components.name: Black sun plate
components.description: The default ground: plywood with the faint red grid.
components.css: .ds-plate { background: linear-gradient(var(--pal-grid) 1px, transparent 1px) 0 0 / 30px 30px, linear-gradient(90deg, var(--pal-grid) 1px, transparent 1px) 0 0 / 30px 30px, var(--pal-plywood); border-radius: 22px; padding: 32px; } .ds-plate-text { color: var(--pal-ink); margin: 0; }

components.name: Black opening plate
components.description: The other ground: ink with a stronger red grid.
components.css: .ds-plate-dark { background: linear-gradient(var(--pal-grid-dark) 1px, transparent 1px) 0 0 / 28px 28px, linear-gradient(90deg, var(--pal-grid-dark) 1px, transparent 1px) 0 0 / 28px 28px, var(--pal-ink); border-radius: 22px; padding: 32px; } .ds-plate-dark-text { color: var(--pal-bone); margin: 0; }

components.name: Star dot
components.description: A code-colour disc with a fine ink ring: a quiet decorative mark until its page exists. Not focusable, hidden from assistive tech, a tap does nothing; a halo ring on a pointer's hover.
components.css: .ds-star { display: inline-block; } .ds-star-halo { opacity: 0; transition: opacity .2s; } @media (hover: hover) { .ds-star:hover .ds-star-halo { opacity: 1; } }

components.name: Sun bands
components.description: The ink ring with its three bands and equal .9 keylines, round the dial.
components.html: <svg class="ds-bands" viewBox="-51 -51 102 102" width="160" height="160" aria-hidden="true"><circle r="35.45" fill="var(--pal-ink)"/><circle r="42.5" fill="none" stroke="var(--pal-ink)" stroke-width="15"/><circle r="38.55" fill="none" stroke="var(--pal-sky)" stroke-width="3.8"/><circle r="43.25" fill="none" stroke="var(--code-events)" stroke-width="3.8"/><circle r="47.95" fill="none" stroke="var(--code-embers)" stroke-width="3.8"/></svg>

components.name: Ground picker
components.description: Two round swatches switching Black sun and Black opening.
components.css: .ds-pick { display: flex; gap: 18px; padding: 9px; background: var(--pal-plywood); } .ds-pick input { appearance: none; margin: 0; width: 18px; height: 18px; border-radius: 50%; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--pal-muted); transition: box-shadow .2s; } .ds-pick-sun { background: radial-gradient(circle, var(--pal-ink) 0 44%, var(--pal-plywood) 47%); } .ds-pick-opening { background: radial-gradient(circle, var(--pal-bone) 0 44%, var(--pal-ink) 47%); } .ds-pick input:checked { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--pal-plywood), 0 0 0 3px var(--pal-ink); } .ds-pick input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--pal-ink); outline-offset: 4px; }

components.name: Words band
components.description: The home's words on a plywood plate, ink text.
components.html: Futures are conspired into existence one word at a time.
components.css: .ds-words { background: var(--pal-plywood); color: var(--pal-ink); padding: 32px; } .ds-words p { margin: 0; }

components.name: Ledger plate
components.description: The ledger on the home and the events page: a black plate, bone titles, bone muted places, ochre upcoming dates; each tag a bone label on a faint bone chip with its initiative's code dot.
components.html:
Tue 3 Nov

components.css: .ds-ledger { background: var(--pal-ink); color: var(--pal-bone); padding: 24px; } .ds-ledger p { margin: 0 0 4px; } .ds-when { color: var(--code-events); font-family: var(--font-mono, monospace); } .ds-where { color: var(--pal-bone-muted); } .ds-kind { font-size: .7rem; letter-spacing: .14em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: .15em .5em; border-radius: 3px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--pal-bone) 12%, var(--pal-ink)); } .ds-kind::before { content: ""; display: inline-block; width: .6em; height: .6em; margin-right: .45em; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--code-events); }

components.name: Compass
components.description: The sun, small, once the sky has scrolled away: a black disc, a bone sigil and ring, each body's dot and needle in its code colour.
components.css: .ds-compass { position: relative; display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 54px; height: 54px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--pal-ink); border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--pal-bone) 28%, transparent); } .ds-compass-ring { position: absolute; inset: 7px; border-radius: 50%; border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--pal-bone) 22%, transparent); } .ds-compass-dot { position: absolute; top: 5px; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--code-embers); }

components.name: Events orrery sun
components.description: The events page's small orrery: a black sun with a bone sigil, ink dashed rings.
components.css: .ds-mini { position: relative; display: inline-block; width: 120px; height: 120px; } .ds-mini-sun { position: absolute; inset: 32%; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--pal-ink); } .ds-mini-ring { position: absolute; inset: 10%; border-radius: 50%; border: 1px dashed color-mix(in srgb, var(--pal-ink) 18%, transparent); }

narrative.overview:
The home opens on an emblem that reads as a slow machine: a black sun with a ticking dial, colour bands, a pyramid with an eye at its centre, and rings that turn against each other like meshed gears. Stopping it is the start of a puzzle: everything settles into one symmetric pose and a seven-point star draws itself behind it.

Colour is a code, not decoration. Each initiative has one colour, and that colour appears only as small solid shapes on quiet neutrals: beige, plywood, ink and bone. A faint red grid under the emblem brings in technique and architecture without shouting.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral grounds, colour only in small solid shapes.
One colour per initiative, the same everywhere it appears.
Ink keylines between colours and around the light ones.
Slow, compositor-only motion; the dial ticks like a seconds hand, backwards.
Two grounds, Black sun (default) and Black opening, picked on the page.

rules.name: The Small Shapes Rule
rules.body: Code colour comes only as small solid shapes: dots, triangles, thin bands. Never a background, a panel or a text block.

rules.name: The Keyline Rule
rules.body: No two code colours meet as fields: an ink keyline (.9) separates the sun's bands. The pyramid is the one drawn object whose faces meet edge to edge; its fine ink outline holds them together.

rules.name: The Light Code Rule
rules.body: Ochre and phosphor take an ink keyline on the beige. Every star dot carries a fine ink ring, so the grey and the green, below 3:1 on plywood, are held the same way.

rules.name: The No Coral Rule
rules.body: No flat warm orange or coral accent on the beige. The red that marks things is the embers red, in small shapes.

rules.name: The Named Colour Rule
rules.body: A code colour that means something is named in text where it leads: each bead's accessible name, and the world it opens.

rules.name: The Contrast Rule
rules.body: Text holds 4.5:1 on its ground; marks hold 3:1, or take an ink keyline.

rules.name: The Reserve Rule
rules.body: Green is kept for things distinct from the main code. It never stands in for an initiative.

rules.name: The Token Rule
rules.body: A new NTS colour, on any page, is a token in section 1 first.

dos: Do take every NTS colour, on every page, from the section 1 tokens.
Do keep code colour to small solid shapes: dots, triangles, thin bands.
Do put an ink keyline between code colours and round ochre and phosphor on the beige.
Do name a code colour in text wherever it means something.
Do hold 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for marks.
Do move only transform and opacity, on whole layers.
donts: Don't use a code colour as a field, a background or body text.
Don't let two code colours touch without a keyline.
Don't put a flat warm orange or coral accent on the beige.
Don't use the reserve green for an initiative.
Don't thicken the pyramid's outline, the eye's border or the dots' rings past the fine tier.
Don't change the emblem's size or position.
